reading.en: Psychology is one of the most popular majors at Israeli universities, and much of its literature is published in English. A classic topic in social psychology is the bystander effect. The term describes the finding that people are less likely to help a stranger when other people are present. In early experiments, participants heard what sounded like someone having a medical emergency in another room. When participants believed they were alone, most of them rushed to help. When they believed several others could also hear, far fewer responded, and those who did took longer. Researchers explained this pattern through a diffusion of responsibility. Each person assumes that someone else will act, so nobody does. Later studies have added important details to this picture. For example, people are more likely to help when the situation is clearly dangerous or when they know the victim. Some recent work even suggests that in real public emergencies, intervention is more common than the laboratory studies predicted. The bystander effect, therefore, is real but more complex than early textbooks implied.

reading.en: Behavioral economics combines insights from psychology and economics. Traditional economic models assumed that people make rational decisions that maximize their own benefit. Behavioral economists, however, have shown that real people often behave in predictable but irrational ways. One famous example is loss aversion, the tendency to feel losses more strongly than equal gains. Losing one hundred shekels usually feels worse than finding one hundred shekels feels good. Another example is the default effect. When employees are automatically enrolled in a pension plan, most of them stay in it, even though they could easily leave. When they must actively choose to join, participation is much lower. Governments have used such findings to design policies known as nudges. A nudge changes the way choices are presented without forbidding any option. Critics argue that nudges can be manipulative, since people may not notice that they are being influenced. Supporters respond that every choice must be presented in some way, so it might as well be designed to help people.

reading.en: Antibiotics are among the most important medical discoveries of the twentieth century. Before they became widely available, simple infections could be fatal. Today, however, scientists warn that their effectiveness is declining because of antibiotic resistance. Resistance develops through natural selection. When a population of bacteria is exposed to a drug, most of them die, but a few may survive because of random mutations. These survivors multiply and pass their resistance on to the next generation. Over time, the drug becomes less and less effective against that species. The process is accelerated when antibiotics are used unnecessarily, for example to treat viral infections such as the common cold. Large-scale use in agriculture, where animals are given antibiotics to promote growth, also contributes to the problem. Some experts predict that resistant infections could cause millions of deaths each year by the middle of the century. To prevent this, doctors are being encouraged to prescribe antibiotics more carefully. At the same time, researchers are searching for entirely new types of drugs.

reading.en: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly used to make decisions that affect people's lives. Banks use them to approve loans, companies use them to screen job applicants, and hospitals use them to detect diseases. Most of these systems are based on machine learning, in which a program learns patterns from large amounts of data. This approach can be extremely powerful, but it also has a serious weakness. If the training data reflect existing social inequalities, the system may learn to reproduce them. In one widely reported case, a hiring algorithm learned to prefer male candidates because most past employees had been men. The developers had never instructed it to discriminate; it simply discovered a pattern in the historical data. Another problem is that many models are difficult to explain. Even their designers may not know exactly why a particular decision was made. This lack of transparency makes it hard to challenge unfair outcomes. Researchers are therefore developing methods for testing algorithms for bias and for making their decisions easier to interpret. Several governments are also preparing laws to regulate the use of AI in sensitive areas.

reading.en: History students quickly learn to distinguish between primary and secondary sources. A primary source is a document or object created during the period being studied, such as a diary, a newspaper or a government report. A secondary source is a later work that analyzes and interprets primary sources, such as a scholarly book. Both types are essential, but they must be read differently. Primary sources offer direct evidence, yet they are never completely neutral. A soldier's letter home may hide the worst experiences in order to protect his family. An official report may present events in a way that favors the government that produced it. Historians therefore ask who created each source, for what purpose and for which audience. They also look for what is missing, since the voices of women, the poor and minorities are often absent from official records. Secondary sources, meanwhile, reflect the questions and concerns of the time in which they were written. A book about the same war may look very different if it was written in 1950 or in 2020. Reading history critically means keeping all of these layers in mind.

reading.en: Legal and political texts are often considered the most difficult to read in English. They contain long sentences, specialized terms and many words borrowed from Latin. Yet the main ideas they discuss are familiar to most citizens. Consider the concept of judicial review, which allows courts to examine whether laws are consistent with a constitution. Supporters argue that this power protects minorities and individual rights from the will of the majority. Without it, they say, a parliament could pass laws that violate basic freedoms. Critics respond that judges are not elected and should not overrule decisions made by the people's representatives. This debate exists in many countries, but it has been particularly intense in Israel, which does not have a complete written constitution. Political scientists study such debates by comparing institutions across countries. They ask, for example, whether strong courts are associated with greater protection of rights or with lower public trust. The answers are rarely simple, since much depends on each country's history and culture. Readers of such texts should therefore watch carefully for the author's own position.

reading.en: Medical research relies heavily on a type of study called the randomized controlled trial. In such a trial, participants are randomly assigned either to receive a new treatment or to receive a placebo. Random assignment ensures that the two groups are similar in age, health and other characteristics. As a result, any difference in outcomes can reasonably be attributed to the treatment itself. In the best trials, neither the patients nor the doctors know who is receiving the real drug. This design, known as double-blind, prevents expectations from influencing the results. Expectations matter more than one might think. Patients who believe they are being treated often report feeling better, even when they have received only a sugar pill. This placebo effect is especially strong for symptoms such as pain and fatigue. Public health researchers, meanwhile, look beyond individual patients to the health of whole populations. They study why some communities have higher rates of disease and which policies, such as clean water or tobacco taxes, can reduce them. Their work shows that a person's address can predict their health almost as well as their genes.

reading.en: Israeli universities require most students to reach an advanced level of English, regardless of their major. The reason is simple: the majority of research in almost every field is published in English. A psychology student will read about experiments, an economics student about markets and a history student about archives. Although the topics differ, the texts share many features. Most of them present a claim, support it with evidence and discuss alternative explanations. They also use hedging, reporting verbs and formal connectors in similar ways. Students who master these general features find it much easier to move between disciplines. At the same time, each field has its own conventions. Scientists value numbers and controlled experiments, while historians value the careful interpretation of documents. Lawyers pay close attention to precise definitions, and computer scientists to step-by-step procedures. A skilled reader adjusts expectations according to the type of text. The ability to read widely across fields is increasingly valuable, since many modern problems require interdisciplinary solutions.
reading.he: אוניברסיטאות בישראל דורשות מרוב הסטודנטים להגיע לרמה מתקדמת באנגלית, בלי קשר למקצוע הלימודים שלהם. הסיבה פשוטה: רוב המחקר כמעט בכל תחום מתפרסם באנגלית. סטודנט/ית לפסיכולוגיה יקרא/תקרא על ניסויים, סטודנט/ית לכלכלה על שווקים וסטודנט/ית להיסטוריה על ארכיונים. אף שהנושאים שונים, לטקסטים יש מאפיינים משותפים רבים. רובם מציגים טענה, תומכים בה בראיות ודנים בהסברים חלופיים. הם גם משתמשים בהסתייגות, בפעלי דיווח ובמילות קישור רשמיות בדרכים דומות. סטודנטים ששולטים במאפיינים הכלליים האלה מוצאים שקל הרבה יותר לעבור בין תחומי דעת. יחד עם זאת, לכל תחום יש מוסכמות משלו. מדענים מעריכים מספרים וניסויים מבוקרים, ואילו היסטוריונים מעריכים פרשנות זהירה של מסמכים. משפטנים שמים לב במיוחד להגדרות מדויקות, ומדעני מחשב להליכים של שלב אחר שלב. קורא/ת מיומן/ת מתאים/ה את הציפיות לפי סוג הטקסט. היכולת לקרוא באופן רחב בין תחומים חשובה יותר ויותר, שכן בעיות מודרניות רבות דורשות פתרונות בין-תחומיים.

reading.en: Few regions illustrate the challenges of water scarcity as clearly as the Middle East. For most of its history, Israel depended on rainfall, the Sea of Galilee and underground aquifers. As the population grew, demand quickly exceeded natural supply, and water levels fell dangerously low. Over the past few decades, however, the country has transformed its water situation. Today, large desalination plants on the Mediterranean coast produce a major share of household drinking water. In addition, most treated wastewater is reused for agriculture, a far higher proportion than in most other countries. Farmers have also adopted drip irrigation, an Israeli invention that delivers water directly to the roots of plants. These developments have turned a chronic shortage into a relative surplus in some years. Nevertheless, the solution is not without costs. Desalination requires large amounts of energy, which may increase greenhouse gas emissions. It also produces salty brine that must be returned to the sea, with possible effects on marine life. Environmental researchers therefore continue to debate how such technologies can be made truly sustainable.

reading.en: Many students study in ways that feel productive but are not very effective. Rereading notes and highlighting textbooks are among the most common strategies. Research suggests, however, that these methods produce only a feeling of familiarity, not deep learning. Two strategies stand out in the scientific literature as particularly powerful. The first is retrieval practice, which means actively recalling information, for example by answering questions without looking at the book. Each act of recall appears to strengthen the memory and make it easier to retrieve later. The second strategy is spaced practice, in which study sessions are spread out over days or weeks. Students who study a topic for one hour on four different days usually remember it far better than those who study for four hours in a single night. Interestingly, many learners believe the opposite, because cramming feels more intense. Another popular belief is that people learn best when teaching matches their preferred learning style. Despite its popularity, this idea has received little support in controlled studies. Education researchers therefore encourage both teachers and students to base their habits on evidence rather than intuition.
reading.he: סטודנטים רבים לומדים בדרכים שמרגישות פרודוקטיביות אך אינן יעילות במיוחד. קריאה חוזרת של סיכומים והדגשה בספרי לימוד הן מהאסטרטגיות הנפוצות ביותר. אולם מחקרים מראים שהשיטות האלה מייצרות רק תחושה של היכרות, לא למידה עמוקה. שתי אסטרטגיות בולטות בספרות המדעית כעוצמתיות במיוחד. הראשונה היא תרגול שליפה, כלומר היזכרות פעילה במידע, למשל על ידי מענה על שאלות בלי להסתכל בספר. נראה שכל פעולת היזכרות מחזקת את הזיכרון ומקלה על שליפתו בהמשך. האסטרטגיה השנייה היא תרגול מרווח, שבו מפגשי הלמידה מפוזרים על פני ימים או שבועות. סטודנטים שלומדים נושא שעה אחת בארבעה ימים שונים זוכרים אותו בדרך כלל הרבה יותר טוב מאלה שלומדים ארבע שעות בלילה אחד. מעניין שלומדים רבים מאמינים בהפך, כי שינון של הרגע האחרון מרגיש אינטנסיבי יותר. אמונה פופולרית נוספת היא שאנשים לומדים הכי טוב כשההוראה מותאמת לסגנון הלמידה המועדף עליהם. למרות הפופולריות שלו, הרעיון הזה זכה לתמיכה מועטה במחקרים מבוקרים. לכן חוקרי חינוך מעודדים מורים וסטודנטים כאחד לבסס את ההרגלים שלהם על ראיות ולא על אינטואיציה.

reading.en: Academic sentences are often long, and their length can intimidate readers. A sentence of forty words may contain several clauses, each adding a layer of information. The key to understanding such sentences is to identify their core: the main subject and the main verb. Consider the sentence 'The policy that the government introduced in 2015, despite strong opposition from teachers, has reduced dropout rates.' Once the extra information is removed, the core is simply 'The policy has reduced dropout rates.' Relative clauses beginning with who, which, that or whose usually describe a noun and can be set aside at first. Phrases between commas often provide background or examples. Readers should also be alert to inverted structures, which place the verb before the subject for emphasis. For example, 'Rarely have such results been reported' means 'Such results have rarely been reported.' Another challenging pattern begins with a clause instead of a noun, as in 'What matters most is consistency.' These structures appear frequently in exemption exams, where questions often test whether students have identified the real subject. With practice, breaking down long sentences becomes almost automatic.
reading.he: משפטים אקדמיים הם לעיתים קרובות ארוכים, והאורך שלהם יכול להרתיע קוראים. משפט של ארבעים מילים עשוי להכיל כמה פסוקיות, שכל אחת מהן מוסיפה שכבת מידע. המפתח להבנת משפטים כאלה הוא לזהות את הליבה שלהם: הנושא העיקרי והפועל העיקרי. חשבו על המשפט 'The policy that the government introduced in 2015, despite strong opposition from teachers, has reduced dropout rates.' כשמסירים את המידע הנוסף, הליבה היא פשוט 'The policy has reduced dropout rates.' פסוקיות זיקה שמתחילות ב-who, which, that או whose מתארות בדרך כלל שם עצם ואפשר להניח אותן בצד בהתחלה. ביטויים שבין פסיקים מספקים לעיתים קרובות רקע או דוגמאות. הקוראים צריכים גם לשים לב למבני היפוך, שמציבים את הפועל לפני הנושא לשם הדגשה. לדוגמה, 'Rarely have such results been reported' פירושו 'Such results have rarely been reported.' דפוס מאתגר נוסף נפתח בפסוקית במקום בשם עצם, כמו ב-'What matters most is consistency.' המבנים האלה מופיעים לעיתים קרובות בבחינות פטור, שבהן השאלות בודקות לעיתים קרובות אם הסטודנטים זיהו את הנושא האמיתי. עם תרגול, פירוק משפטים ארוכים הופך לכמעט אוטומטי.

reading.en: Reading comprehension questions can be divided into two broad types. Some questions ask about information that is stated directly in the text. Others ask readers to make inferences, that is, to draw conclusions that the text supports but does not state. Inference questions are usually considered more difficult, and they appear frequently in university exams. Imagine a passage that says a new museum attracted far fewer visitors than planned and that its director resigned after one year. The text may never say that the museum was a failure. Nevertheless, a reader can reasonably infer that its first year did not meet expectations. A common mistake is to choose an answer that seems logical but relies on outside knowledge. For example, concluding that the director was dismissed would go beyond the evidence, since the passage says only that she resigned. Good inferences stay close to the text and can be justified by pointing to specific words or sentences. Writers' word choices often provide important clues. Words such as 'surprisingly', 'merely' and 'unfortunately' reveal attitudes that are not stated openly.
reading.he: שאלות הבנת הנקרא אפשר לחלק לשני סוגים רחבים. שאלות מסוימות שואלות על מידע שמופיע במפורש בטקסט. אחרות מבקשות מהקוראים להסיק מסקנות, כלומר להגיע למסקנות שהטקסט תומך בהן אך אינו אומר אותן. שאלות הסקה נחשבות בדרך כלל קשות יותר, והן מופיעות לעיתים קרובות בבחינות באוניברסיטה. דמיינו קטע שאומר שמוזיאון חדש משך הרבה פחות מבקרים מהמתוכנן ושהמנהלת שלו התפטרה אחרי שנה. ייתכן שהטקסט לעולם לא יאמר שהמוזיאון נכשל. ובכל זאת, הקורא יכול להסיק באופן סביר שהשנה הראשונה שלו לא עמדה בציפיות. טעות נפוצה היא לבחור תשובה שנראית הגיונית אך מסתמכת על ידע חיצוני. לדוגמה, מסקנה שהמנהלת פוטרה תחרוג מהראיות, כי הקטע אומר רק שהיא התפטרה. הסקות טובות נשארות קרובות לטקסט ואפשר להצדיק אותן בהצבעה על מילים או משפטים ספציפיים. בחירות המילים של הכותבים מספקות לעיתים קרובות רמזים חשובים. מילים כמו 'surprisingly', 'merely' ו-'unfortunately' חושפות עמדות שאינן נאמרות בגלוי.

reading.en: Every text is written for a reason, and recognizing that reason is an essential reading skill. Some texts aim to inform, presenting facts in a neutral way. Others aim to persuade, trying to convince readers to accept a position or take action. The purpose of a text is closely connected to its tone, which is the attitude the writer expresses toward the subject. Tone is created mainly through word choice. A writer who describes a policy as 'bold' has a different attitude from one who calls the same policy 'reckless'. Exam questions often ask about tone by offering adjectives such as objective, critical, optimistic or ironic. To answer correctly, readers should look for evaluative words and notice which side of an issue receives more space. Questions about purpose may also focus on a single paragraph or example. In such cases, it helps to ask what the paragraph contributes to the whole text. Does it give background, provide evidence, present an opposing view or offer a solution? Thinking about function rather than content usually leads to the right answer.
reading.he: כל טקסט נכתב מסיבה מסוימת, וזיהוי הסיבה הזו הוא מיומנות קריאה חיונית. טקסטים מסוימים נועדו ליידע, ומציגים עובדות באופן ניטרלי. אחרים נועדו לשכנע, ומנסים לשכנע את הקוראים לקבל עמדה או לפעול. מטרת הטקסט קשורה קשר הדוק לטון שלו, כלומר לעמדה שהכותב מביע כלפי הנושא. הטון נוצר בעיקר באמצעות בחירת מילים. כותב שמתאר מדיניות כ'נועזת' מחזיק בעמדה שונה מזה שמכנה את אותה מדיניות 'פזיזה'. שאלות בבחינות שואלות לעיתים קרובות על הטון באמצעות שמות תואר כמו objective, critical, optimistic או ironic. כדי לענות נכון, הקוראים צריכים לחפש מילים מעריכות ולשים לב איזה צד של הסוגיה מקבל יותר מקום. שאלות על מטרה עשויות גם להתמקד בפסקה או בדוגמה אחת. במקרים כאלה, עוזר לשאול מה הפסקה תורמת לטקסט כולו. האם היא נותנת רקע, מספקת ראיות, מציגה עמדה מנוגדת או מציעה פתרון? חשיבה על התפקיד ולא על התוכן מובילה בדרך כלל לתשובה הנכונה.

reading.en: Tables and figures allow researchers to present large amounts of data in a compact form. A well-designed graph can reveal a trend more quickly than several paragraphs of text. However, visual information can also mislead, sometimes deliberately. One common technique is to start the vertical axis at a value other than zero. A graph showing an increase from 50 to 52 percent will look dramatic if the axis begins at 49. Readers who glance quickly may conclude that the change was enormous. Another problem arises when two graphs that are meant to be compared use different scales. In addition, a graph may show a strong correlation between two variables without proving that one causes the other. Careful readers therefore begin by reading the title, the labels on each axis and the units. They then look for the source of the data and the size of the sample. Only after these checks do they interpret the trend itself. These habits are useful not only in academic reading but also when following the news.
reading.he: טבלאות ותרשימים מאפשרים לחוקרים להציג כמויות גדולות של נתונים בצורה תמציתית. גרף מתוכנן היטב יכול לחשוף מגמה מהר יותר מכמה פסקאות טקסט. עם זאת, מידע חזותי יכול גם להטעות, לפעמים בכוונה. טכניקה נפוצה אחת היא להתחיל את הציר האנכי בערך שאינו אפס. גרף שמראה עלייה מ-50 ל-52 אחוז ייראה דרמטי אם הציר מתחיל ב-49. קוראים שמעיפים מבט מהיר עשויים להסיק שהשינוי היה עצום. בעיה נוספת מתעוררת כששני גרפים שאמורים להיות מושווים משתמשים בקני מידה שונים. בנוסף, גרף עשוי להראות מתאם חזק בין שני משתנים בלי להוכיח שאחד גורם לשני. לכן קוראים זהירים מתחילים בקריאת הכותרת, התוויות על כל ציר והיחידות. אחר כך הם מחפשים את מקור הנתונים ואת גודל המדגם. רק אחרי הבדיקות האלה הם מפרשים את המגמה עצמה. ההרגלים האלה שימושיים לא רק בקריאה אקדמית אלא גם במעקב אחר החדשות.

reading.en: Israeli universities require students to demonstrate a certain level of English, usually through a national exam such as the Amir or the Amiram. Students who score high enough are exempt from English courses, while others must complete one or more levels. The exam typically includes sentence completion, restatement and reading comprehension sections. Each section rewards specific strategies. In sentence completion, students should first identify the logical relationship in the sentence, such as contrast or cause. A sentence beginning with 'Although' will usually require an answer that contrasts with the first clause. In restatement questions, the correct answer often uses different vocabulary and structure but keeps exactly the same meaning. Wrong answers may be very similar in wording yet change a small but crucial detail. In reading comprehension, time management is essential. Many test-takers recommend reading the questions first so that they know what to look for. Because there is no penalty for wrong answers, students should never leave a question blank. Above all, regular practice with authentic materials is the most reliable way to improve.

reading.en: Rotem was preparing for her English exemption exam, and she decided to practice with a passage about urban gardens. The text described a project in which residents of a poor neighborhood turned empty lots into vegetable gardens. According to the author, the project improved residents' diets and created a stronger sense of community. However, the author added that the gardens depended almost entirely on volunteers. In the final paragraph, the writer noted that two of the five gardens had closed after the main organizer moved away. The first question asked about the main idea, and Rotem chose the answer about community benefits. The second question asked what could be inferred about the project's future. Rotem noticed that the text never said the project would fail. Nevertheless, the information about volunteers and closed gardens suggested that it might not survive without stable support. She selected that answer and checked that every part of it was supported by the text. The third question asked about the author's tone, and she chose 'cautiously positive'. When she checked the answer key, she found that she had answered all three questions correctly.

reading.en: Group projects are a common feature of university courses, especially in business, engineering and the social sciences. Lecturers assign them because teamwork is an essential skill in most professions. Students, however, often have mixed feelings about working in groups. A frequent complaint is that the workload is not shared fairly. In many teams, one or two motivated members end up doing most of the work, while others contribute little. This problem, sometimes called social loafing, has been studied by psychologists for decades. Research shows that it is more likely when individual contributions are hard to identify. Clear roles and deadlines can therefore reduce the problem significantly. Many successful groups begin by writing a short agreement that lists each member's responsibilities. They also use shared documents, which make it easy to see who has written what. Some lecturers ask students to evaluate their teammates at the end of the project, and these evaluations influence individual grades. Although group work can be frustrating, students who learn to manage it well gain experience that employers value highly.

reading.en: Academic conferences bring together researchers to share new work and discuss ideas. For graduate students, presenting at a conference is often the first step into the professional academic world. The process usually begins with a call for papers, in which organizers invite researchers to submit abstracts. A committee then reviews the abstracts and decides which will be presented as talks and which as posters. Some students are disappointed to receive a poster slot, but posters have real advantages. Instead of speaking to a silent audience, presenters have one-to-one conversations with interested visitors. These conversations often lead to useful feedback and new professional contacts. An effective poster is visual and easy to scan from a distance. It should highlight the research question, the method, the key findings and a clear conclusion. Presenters should also prepare a short spoken summary, since many visitors will ask for one. Talks, by contrast, require careful timing, because chairs strictly enforce time limits. In both formats, the ability to answer questions calmly is just as important as the presentation itself.

reading.en: Peer review is the process by which experts evaluate research before it is published. When a researcher submits an article to a journal, the editor sends it to two or three specialists in the field. These reviewers usually remain anonymous, which allows them to be honest without fear of consequences. They assess whether the research question is important, whether the methods are sound and whether the conclusions follow from the data. The editor then decides to accept the paper, reject it or ask for revisions. Very few articles are accepted without any changes. Peer review is considered one of the foundations of scientific quality, yet it is far from perfect. Reviewers are busy, unpaid and sometimes biased against ideas that challenge their own work. Some fraudulent studies have passed peer review, while some important discoveries were initially rejected. Many universities now teach students to give peer feedback on each other's essays. This practice helps students see their own writing through a reader's eyes. It also teaches them to give criticism that is specific, respectful and constructive.
reading.he: שיפוט עמיתים הוא התהליך שבו מומחים מעריכים מחקר לפני שהוא מתפרסם. כשחוקר/ת מגיש/ה מאמר לכתב עת, העורך שולח אותו לשניים או שלושה מומחים בתחום. השופטים האלה נשארים בדרך כלל אנונימיים, וזה מאפשר להם להיות כנים בלי לחשוש מהשלכות. הם מעריכים אם שאלת המחקר חשובה, אם השיטות תקינות ואם המסקנות נובעות מהנתונים. אחר כך העורך מחליט לקבל את המאמר, לדחות אותו או לבקש תיקונים. מעט מאוד מאמרים מתקבלים בלי שינויים כלשהם. שיפוט עמיתים נחשב לאחד מיסודות האיכות המדעית, אך הוא רחוק מלהיות מושלם. השופטים עסוקים, אינם מקבלים תשלום ולפעמים מוטים נגד רעיונות שמערערים על עבודתם שלהם. כמה מחקרים מזויפים עברו שיפוט עמיתים, ואילו כמה תגליות חשובות נדחו בתחילה. אוניברסיטאות רבות מלמדות כיום סטודנטים לתת משוב עמיתים על חיבורים של חבריהם. הנוהג הזה עוזר לסטודנטים לראות את הכתיבה שלהם דרך עיני הקורא. הוא גם מלמד אותם לתת ביקורת ספציפית, מכבדת ובונה.

reading.en: Many students finish writing their essays just before the deadline and submit them without revision. This habit costs them points, because even strong ideas lose force when they are full of errors. Experienced writers distinguish between two stages of revision. Editing comes first and deals with larger issues: the clarity of the argument, the order of paragraphs and the strength of the evidence. Proofreading comes last and focuses on spelling, punctuation and grammar. Doing these tasks in the wrong order wastes time, since a carefully proofread paragraph may later be deleted. Second-language writers often have typical error patterns that are worth checking systematically. Hebrew and Arabic speakers, for example, frequently omit or misuse the articles 'a' and 'the'. Russian speakers face a similar difficulty, since Russian has no articles at all. Other common problems include subject-verb agreement and the choice between past simple and present perfect. Keeping a personal list of one's most frequent mistakes can make proofreading much more efficient. Digital tools are helpful, but they should support the writer's judgment rather than replace it.

reading.en: Before beginning a thesis or applying for a research grant, students are usually asked to write a research proposal. A proposal is essentially a persuasive document: it must convince readers that the project is important, original and achievable. Most proposals follow a familiar structure. They open by introducing the problem and explaining why it matters. A short literature review then shows what is already known and identifies the gap the project will address. Next comes the research question, followed by a description of the planned methods. Many proposals also include a timeline, a budget and a discussion of ethical issues. Reviewers often reject proposals not because the idea is poor but because the plan is unrealistic. A master's student who promises to interview five hundred people in six months may raise doubts about feasibility. Similarly, vague methods suggest that the writer has not thought the project through. Proposals are written in the future tense, since they describe work that has not yet been done. Writing a strong proposal takes time, but it also clarifies the project for the researcher.
reading.he: לפני תחילת עבודת תזה או הגשת בקשה למענק מחקר, סטודנטים מתבקשים בדרך כלל לכתוב הצעת מחקר. הצעה היא בעיקרה מסמך משכנע: היא חייבת לשכנע את הקוראים שהפרויקט חשוב, מקורי וניתן לביצוע. רוב ההצעות עוקבות אחר מבנה מוכר. הן נפתחות בהצגת הבעיה ובהסבר מדוע היא חשובה. אחר כך סקירת ספרות קצרה מראה מה כבר ידוע ומזהה את הפער שהפרויקט יעסוק בו. לאחר מכן באה שאלת המחקר, ואחריה תיאור השיטות המתוכננות. הצעות רבות כוללות גם לוח זמנים, תקציב ודיון בסוגיות אתיות. השופטים דוחים לעיתים קרובות הצעות לא משום שהרעיון חלש אלא משום שהתוכנית אינה מציאותית. סטודנט/ית לתואר שני שמבטיח/ה לראיין חמש מאות איש בתוך שישה חודשים עלול/ה לעורר ספקות לגבי ישימות. באופן דומה, שיטות מעורפלות מרמזות שהכותב לא חשב על הפרויקט עד הסוף. הצעות נכתבות בזמן עתיד, שכן הן מתארות עבודה שעדיין לא נעשתה. כתיבת הצעה חזקה דורשת זמן, אבל היא גם מבהירה את הפרויקט לחוקר/ת עצמו/ה.

reading.en: For graduate students, the relationship with a supervisor is one of the most important factors in completing a degree successfully. A supervisor guides the research, comments on drafts and often helps the student enter the academic community. Choosing the right person is therefore a significant decision. Students should consider not only the supervisor's expertise but also his or her style of working. Some supervisors meet their students every week and read every page in detail. Others prefer to give students considerable independence and meet only once a month. Neither style is better in itself, but a mismatch between expectations can cause frustration. It is wise to discuss these expectations openly at the start, including how often to meet and how quickly feedback will be returned. Students also share responsibility for the relationship. Arriving at meetings with specific questions and a short summary of progress makes the time far more productive. When problems arise, such as delays or personal difficulties, it is usually better to report them early than to disappear. Most supervisors are understanding, but they cannot help with problems they do not know about.
reading.he: עבור סטודנטים לתארים מתקדמים, הקשר עם המנחה הוא אחד הגורמים החשובים ביותר בהשלמת התואר בהצלחה. המנחה מכוון/ת את המחקר, מעיר/ה על טיוטות ולעיתים קרובות עוזר/ת לסטודנט/ית להיכנס לקהילה האקדמית. לכן בחירת האדם הנכון היא החלטה משמעותית. הסטודנטים צריכים לשקול לא רק את המומחיות של המנחה אלא גם את סגנון העבודה שלו או שלה. יש מנחים שנפגשים עם הסטודנטים שלהם כל שבוע וקוראים כל עמוד בפירוט. אחרים מעדיפים לתת לסטודנטים עצמאות רבה ולהיפגש רק פעם בחודש. אף סגנון אינו טוב יותר כשלעצמו, אבל אי-התאמה בין ציפיות עלולה לגרום לתסכול. נבון לדון בציפיות האלה בגלוי כבר בהתחלה, כולל באיזו תדירות להיפגש וכמה מהר יוחזר משוב. גם הסטודנטים נושאים באחריות לקשר. הגעה לפגישות עם שאלות ספציפיות וסיכום קצר של ההתקדמות הופכת את הזמן לפרודוקטיבי הרבה יותר. כשמתעוררות בעיות, כמו עיכובים או קשיים אישיים, בדרך כלל עדיף לדווח עליהן מוקדם מאשר להיעלם. רוב המנחים מגלים הבנה, אבל הם אינם יכולים לעזור בבעיות שהם לא יודעים עליהן.

reading.en: Few developments have affected universities as quickly as generative artificial intelligence. Within a short time, tools that can write essays, summarize articles and solve problems became available to every student. Reactions in the academic world have ranged from enthusiasm to alarm. Some lecturers initially banned AI tools entirely, fearing that students would stop learning to think and write. Others have welcomed them as a new kind of learning assistant, similar to a calculator for writing. Most institutions now take a middle path, allowing certain uses while forbidding others. Using AI to explain a difficult concept or to check grammar is often permitted, especially if it is disclosed. Submitting a text generated entirely by AI, however, is usually treated as academic misconduct. A further problem is accuracy. AI systems can produce convincing but false information, including citations to articles that do not exist. Students who rely on such output without checking it risk serious errors. Many educators argue that the real challenge is to design assignments that reward the skills AI cannot easily replace, such as personal reflection and original analysis.
reading.he: מעט התפתחויות השפיעו על האוניברסיטאות מהר כמו הבינה המלאכותית היוצרת. בתוך זמן קצר, כלים שיכולים לכתוב חיבורים, לסכם מאמרים ולפתור בעיות הפכו לזמינים לכל סטודנט/ית. התגובות בעולם האקדמי נעו בין התלהבות לבהלה. יש מרצים שבתחילה אסרו לחלוטין על כלי בינה מלאכותית, מחשש שהסטודנטים יפסיקו ללמוד לחשוב ולכתוב. אחרים קיבלו אותם בברכה כסוג חדש של עוזר למידה, בדומה למחשבון לכתיבה. רוב המוסדות נוקטים כיום דרך ביניים, ומתירים שימושים מסוימים תוך איסור על אחרים. שימוש בבינה מלאכותית כדי להסביר מושג קשה או לבדוק דקדוק מותר לעיתים קרובות, במיוחד אם מצהירים עליו. אולם הגשת טקסט שנוצר כולו על ידי בינה מלאכותית נחשבת בדרך כלל להתנהגות אקדמית פסולה. בעיה נוספת היא דיוק. מערכות בינה מלאכותית יכולות להפיק מידע משכנע אך שגוי, כולל ציטוטים של מאמרים שאינם קיימים. סטודנטים שמסתמכים על תוצרים כאלה בלי לבדוק אותם מסתכנים בטעויות חמורות. אנשי חינוך רבים טוענים שהאתגר האמיתי הוא לתכנן מטלות שמתגמלות את המיומנויות שבינה מלאכותית אינה יכולה להחליף בקלות, כמו רפלקציה אישית וניתוח מקורי.

reading.en: Lior, a master's student in environmental science, spent a year preparing her first major research project. She began by writing a proposal on the effects of urban heat on elderly residents in southern Israel. Her supervisor praised the topic but warned that the original plan was too ambitious. Together they reduced the number of neighborhoods from ten to four and extended the timeline. Lior also used an AI tool to help her find relevant studies. Although it saved time, she discovered that several of the suggested references did not exist, so she checked every source carefully. Halfway through the project, she presented her preliminary results as a poster at a national conference. Visitors asked difficult questions about her measurement methods, which led her to add a second type of temperature sensor. When she finally submitted an article to a journal, the reviewers requested major revisions. Lior was disappointed at first, but she addressed each comment systematically. The revised article was accepted six months later. She now advises new students to see criticism as part of the process rather than as a personal failure.

reading.en: Applying to graduate school requires much more than good grades. Most programs ask for a statement of purpose, letters of recommendation, a CV and, in some cases, a writing sample. The statement of purpose is often the most challenging part, especially when it must be written in English. It should explain the applicant's academic background, research interests and reasons for choosing that particular program. Admissions committees read hundreds of statements, so generic texts are quickly forgotten. A strong statement tells a coherent story that connects past experience with future goals. For example, an applicant might describe how a seminar on migration inspired her to study refugee education. She would then explain which faculty members' work matches her interests and why. Letters of recommendation are equally important. Committees value letters from lecturers who know the applicant's work well over letters from famous professors who barely remember the student. This is another reason why building relationships through office hours and seminars pays off. Finally, applicants should start early, since gathering all the documents usually takes several months.

reading.en: Financial support can make the difference between continuing one's studies and dropping out. In Israel, students can apply for scholarships from universities, government bodies, private foundations and local authorities. Some scholarships reward academic excellence, while others are based on financial need or social involvement. Many require recipients to volunteer a certain number of hours each year in schools or community centers. Applications usually ask for a CV, grade transcripts and a personal statement. An academic CV differs from a standard job résumé in several ways. It focuses on education, research experience, publications, presentations, teaching and awards. Unlike a business résumé, it is not limited to one or two pages and grows longer as a career develops. Students at the beginning of their studies may feel that they have little to include. However, research assistant positions, seminar papers and volunteer work can all be presented effectively. The key is to describe each item precisely and to keep the format consistent. A well-organized CV suggests the same careful thinking that committees hope to see in future research.

reading.en: Every year, thousands of Israeli students spend a semester or a year studying at a university abroad. Exchange programs allow them to take courses at partner institutions while remaining enrolled at their home university. Students improve their language skills, gain independence and learn to see their own field from a different perspective. Employers also tend to value international experience, since it suggests adaptability and openness. Nevertheless, studying abroad is not always easy. Many students go through a period of culture shock, in which initial excitement gives way to homesickness and frustration. Academic expectations can be surprisingly different as well. In some countries, students are expected to participate actively in every class, while in others they are graded mainly on a single final exam. Some Israeli students are surprised by how formally lecturers are addressed in certain European universities. Preparation helps considerably. Students who research the academic culture in advance and connect with former exchange students usually adapt more quickly. Most participants report that, despite the difficulties, the experience was one of the most valuable parts of their degree.

reading.en: Most students do not stay in academia after graduation, so universities increasingly emphasize preparation for the job market. Internships are one of the most effective ways to bridge the gap between study and work. They allow students to apply academic knowledge in real settings and to discover which careers suit them. In Israel, many students already work during their degree, often in jobs unrelated to their field. Although such jobs provide income, they may not offer the professional experience that employers seek. Career advisers therefore encourage students to look for positions that build relevant skills, even if they pay less. Another key concept is transferable skills. These are abilities developed in one context that remain useful in another. A history student, for example, learns to analyze large amounts of information, evaluate sources and write clearly. These skills are valuable in journalism, law, public policy and many other fields. The challenge is to describe them convincingly in a CV and an interview. Instead of writing 'I wrote a seminar paper,' a graduate might explain that she 'researched, organized and presented a forty-page analysis under a strict deadline.'

reading.en: In recent years, the scientific community has faced what is often called the replication crisis. When researchers tried to repeat well-known experiments in psychology and medicine, many of the original results could not be reproduced. Several factors seem to explain this problem. Journals have traditionally preferred surprising, positive findings, so studies that found nothing were rarely published. Researchers, under pressure to publish, sometimes analyzed their data in many different ways until a significant result appeared. Small samples also made chance findings more likely. In response, a movement known as open science has gained strength. Its supporters argue that research should be transparent at every stage. They encourage scientists to pre-register their hypotheses and methods before collecting data, which makes it harder to change the plan after seeing the results. They also promote the sharing of raw data and analysis code, so that others can check the work. Another goal is open access, which allows anyone to read research articles without paying high subscription fees. Not everyone agrees on how far these reforms should go, but most researchers accept that greater transparency strengthens trust in science.

reading.en: For a long time, many scientists saw communicating with the public as a distraction from serious research. Funding agencies increasingly expect researchers to explain the value of their work to taxpayers. Public health crises have also shown how important it is for citizens to understand scientific evidence. Yet communicating science well is surprisingly difficult. Researchers are trained to speak precisely to other experts, using technical terms and careful qualifications. A general audience, by contrast, needs clear language, concrete examples and a sense of why the topic matters. The media add a further complication. A cautious finding such as 'coffee may be associated with a slightly lower risk of certain diseases' can quickly become the headline 'Coffee prevents disease.' Such exaggerations damage trust when later studies fail to confirm them. Good science communicators therefore explain not only what was found but also how certain the finding is. They distinguish between a single study and a broad scientific consensus. For students, practicing these skills is valuable, since explaining an idea simply is often the best test of truly understanding it.
reading.he: במשך זמן רב, מדענים רבים ראו בתקשורת עם הציבור הסחת דעת ממחקר רציני. גופים מממנים מצפים יותר ויותר מהחוקרים להסביר למשלמי המסים את ערך עבודתם. משברי בריאות ציבורית גם הראו עד כמה חשוב שהאזרחים יבינו ראיות מדעיות. ובכל זאת, תקשורת מדע טובה קשה באופן מפתיע. חוקרים מוכשרים לדבר בדיוק אל מומחים אחרים, תוך שימוש במונחים טכניים ובהסתייגויות זהירות. קהל רחב, לעומת זאת, זקוק לשפה ברורה, לדוגמאות קונקרטיות ולתחושה מדוע הנושא חשוב. התקשורת מוסיפה סיבוך נוסף. ממצא זהיר כמו 'coffee may be associated with a slightly lower risk of certain diseases' יכול להפוך במהירות לכותרת 'Coffee prevents disease.' הגזמות כאלה פוגעות באמון כשמחקרים מאוחרים יותר אינם מאששים אותן. לכן מתקשרי מדע טובים מסבירים לא רק מה נמצא אלא גם עד כמה הממצא ודאי. הם מבחינים בין מחקר יחיד לבין הסכמה מדעית רחבה. עבור סטודנטים, תרגול המיומנויות האלה הוא בעל ערך, שכן הסבר פשוט של רעיון הוא לעיתים קרובות המבחן הטוב ביותר להבנה אמיתית שלו.

reading.en: In the past, people often studied for a few years and then worked in the same profession for the rest of their lives. That model no longer describes the reality of most careers. New technologies are transforming industries, and some jobs that exist today may disappear within a generation. At the same time, new professions are emerging that did not exist when today's graduates started school. In this environment, the ability to keep learning has become as important as any specific body of knowledge. Universities are responding by offering short professional programs, evening courses and online certificates for adults. Many Israelis now return to study in their thirties, forties or even later. However, lifelong learning is not only about formal courses. It also involves habits such as reading widely, asking questions and reflecting on experience. In this sense, the skills practiced in academic English courses have lasting value. A person who can read a research article critically, summarize its main points and evaluate its evidence can continue learning in any field. Perhaps the most important lesson of university, then, is not a particular fact but the confidence to keep discovering new ones.
reading.he: בעבר, אנשים למדו לעיתים קרובות כמה שנים ואז עבדו באותו מקצוע במשך כל חייהם. המודל הזה כבר אינו מתאר את המציאות של רוב הקריירות. טכנולוגיות חדשות משנות תעשיות, ויש משרות שקיימות היום שעשויות להיעלם בתוך דור אחד. במקביל, צצים מקצועות חדשים שלא היו קיימים כשבוגרי היום התחילו את בית הספר. בסביבה כזו, היכולת להמשיך ללמוד הפכה לחשובה כמו כל גוף ידע ספציפי. האוניברסיטאות מגיבות בכך שהן מציעות תוכניות מקצועיות קצרות, קורסי ערב ותעודות מקוונות למבוגרים. ישראלים רבים חוזרים כיום ללימודים בשנות השלושים, הארבעים או אפילו מאוחר יותר. עם זאת, למידה לאורך החיים אינה עוסקת רק בקורסים פורמליים. היא כוללת גם הרגלים כמו קריאה רחבה, שאילת שאלות והתבוננות בחוויות. במובן הזה, למיומנויות שמתרגלים בקורסי אנגלית אקדמית יש ערך מתמשך. אדם שיודע לקרוא מאמר מחקר באופן ביקורתי, לסכם את נקודותיו העיקריות ולהעריך את הראיות שבו יכול להמשיך ללמוד בכל תחום. אם כן, ייתכן שהלקח החשוב ביותר של האוניברסיטה אינו עובדה מסוימת אלא הביטחון להמשיך לגלות עובדות חדשות.

reading.en: At the end of her first year, Shira looked back at how much her academic English had changed. In October, she had struggled to follow lectures and had avoided asking questions. She had copied whole sentences into her notes and had felt lost when reading research articles. Over the year, she learned to skim abstracts, identify thesis statements and notice hedging words. She discovered that reporting verbs such as 'claims' and 'demonstrates' revealed an author's attitude toward a source. In her seminar on public health, she evaluated a study whose impressive results were based on a small, unrepresentative sample. She pointed out this limitation in a class discussion, softening her criticism with phrases she had practiced. Her final paper compared two policies for reducing smoking among teenagers. It opened with a clear thesis, included a counterargument and ended with suggestions for future research. Her lecturer noted that the paper was well structured, carefully referenced and written in an appropriate academic register. Shira also passed her exemption exam, which allowed her to take advanced courses taught entirely in English. She concluded that the greatest change was not in her vocabulary but in the way she now read and thought.
reading.he: בסוף השנה הראשונה שלה, שירה הביטה לאחור וראתה כמה השתנתה האנגלית האקדמית שלה. באוקטובר היא התקשתה לעקוב אחר הרצאות ונמנעה משאילת שאלות. היא העתיקה משפטים שלמים לסיכומים שלה והרגישה אבודה כשקראה מאמרי מחקר. במהלך השנה היא למדה לרפרף על תקצירים, לזהות הצהרות תזה ולשים לב למילות הסתייגות. היא גילתה שפעלי דיווח כמו 'claims' ו-'demonstrates' חושפים את עמדת המחבר כלפי מקור. בסמינר שלה בבריאות הציבור היא העריכה מחקר שתוצאותיו המרשימות התבססו על מדגם קטן ולא מייצג. היא הצביעה על המגבלה הזו בדיון בכיתה, וריככה את הביקורת שלה בביטויים שתרגלה. העבודה הסופית שלה השוותה בין שתי מדיניות לצמצום העישון בקרב בני נוער. היא נפתחה בתזה ברורה, כללה טיעון נגדי והסתיימה בהצעות למחקר עתידי. המרצה שלה ציינה שהעבודה בנויה היטב, מתועדת בקפידה וכתובה במשלב אקדמי מתאים. שירה גם עברה את בחינת הפטור, מה שאפשר לה ללמוד קורסים מתקדמים שמועברים כולם באנגלית. היא הסיקה שהשינוי הגדול ביותר לא היה באוצר המילים שלה אלא בדרך שבה היא קוראת וחושבת עכשיו.
